You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# ARC template stamping

Use this when a demo shows a distinctive compact colored object and many single-cell markers on a background, and the output repeats the object around each marker.

1. Identify the background, the source template object, and the marker color by comparing demo input/output. The source template is usually a small rectangular pattern whose background-colored cells are transparent.
2. Determine the anchor cell of the template from the demonstration: commonly a central template cell maps onto each marker. Check this using multiple markers, including those near edges.
3. For each marker in the test grid, copy the template's non-background cells with the same relative offsets, centered/aligned on the marker; replace the marker as part of the stamp. Preserve all unrelated background and preserve the original source object unless the demonstration shows otherwise.
4. If stamps overlap, infer precedence from the demo and apply it consistently. Ensure grid dimensions stay unchanged and clip only if edge behavior is demonstrated.

Worked pattern from task-76eceeef: a 3x3 template with rows `[bg,5,5]`, `[8,5,8]`, `[8,5,0]` is centered on every marker cell (color 1), replacing each marker; the seed template remains.
